content:         1→# Specification: Corriger diagnostics de subprocess dans assertSuccess et requireSuccess
        2→
        3→## Problem Statement
        4→
        5→Les méthodes privées `assertSuccess` (runtime.ts:681-686) et `requireSuccess` (gitPromotion.ts:523-530) masquent le stdout lorsque stderr est présent. Le code actuel utilise `result.stderr.trim() || result.stdout.trim()` qui retourne uniquement stderr si non-vide, ignorant complètement stdout même si celui-ci contient des informations diagnostiques importantes.
        6→
        7→## Solution
        8→
        9→Corriger le formatage des messages d'erreur pour afficher les deux flux (stderr et stdout) de manière distincte et complète, avec stderr en premier si non-vide, suivi de stdout si non-vide. Utiliser le format : `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>`. Si les deux flux sont vides, afficher `Unable to <action>: exit code N`.
       10→
       11→## User Stories
       12→
       13→1. As a developer, I want to see both stderr and stdout error messages from subprocess failures, so that I can diagnose issues more effectively without missing critical information
       14→2. As a maintainer, I want stderr to be displayed before stdout in error messages, so that error streams follow conventional logging practices
       15→3. As a tester, I want empty streams to be excluded from error messages, so that I only see relevant diagnostic information
       16→4. As a user, I want to see the exit code when both streams are empty, so that I have minimal diagnostic information for the failure
       17→5. As a developer, I want success cases to remain unchanged, so that existing behavior is preserved for non-error scenarios
       18→
       19→## Implementation Decisions
       20→
       21→- **Error message format**: `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>` with real newline character between streams
       22→- **Display order**: stderr first if non-empty, then stdout if non-empty
       23→- **Stream filtering**: Only include non-empty trimmed streams in the error message
       24→- **Fallback behavior**: `Unable to <action>: exit code N` when both stderr and stdout are empty
       25→- **Success preservation**: No changes to success case handling
       26→- **Method preservation**: All private methods and interfaces remain unchanged; no duplication, truncation, or deduplication
       27→- **File scope**: Changes limited to `acp-sandbox/src/runtime.ts` (assertSuccess) and `acp-sandbox/src/gitPromotion.ts` (requireSuccess)
       28→
       29→## Testing Decisions
       30→
       31→- **Test location**: `acp-sandbox/test/runtime.test.ts`
       32→- **Test approach**: 5 public API tests for `runCodex` using `fakeExecutor`/`sandboxScenario`
       33→- **Test coverage**:
       34→  1. Two streams (both stderr and stdout non-empty)
       35→  2. Stderr only (stdout empty)
       36→  3. Stdout only (stderr empty)
       37→  4. No streams (both empty)
       38→  5. Success case (no error)
       39→- **Existing tests**: Update affected expectations in runtime and promotion tests to match new error message format
       40→- **Execution**: `npm ci` at root then `npm test` at root with real exit codes
       41→
       42→## Out of Scope
       43→
       44→- No changes to private/any access modifiers
       45→- No package.json/lock/dependency modifications
       46→- No ADR or glossary updates
       47→- No tail/pipefail/tsx usage
       48→- No historical audits or transcriptions
       49→- No duplication of existing functionality
       50→
       51→## Further Notes
       52→
       53→- Pipeline: Full complete pipeline execution required
       54→- Verification: Targeted review of diff from BASE and approved docs only
       55→- Artifacts: T01 JSON object acp.implementation-result/v1; acp.verification-report/v1 review
       56→- Single vertical ticket in `.scratch/corriger-diagnostics-subprocess/`
       57→- All changes must preserve existing private method signatures and interfaces

content:         1→# Specification: Corriger diagnostics de subprocess dans assertSuccess et requireSuccess
        2→
        3→## Problem Statement
        4→
        5→Les méthodes privées `assertSuccess` (runtime.ts:681-686) et `requireSuccess` (gitPromotion.ts:523-530) masquent le stdout lorsque stderr est présent. Le code actuel utilise `result.stderr.trim() || result.stdout.trim()` qui retourne uniquement stderr si non-vide, ignorant complètement stdout même si celui-ci contient des informations diagnostiques importantes.
        6→
        7→## Solution
        8→
        9→Corriger le formatage des messages d'erreur pour afficher les deux flux (stderr et stdout) de manière distincte et complète, avec stderr en premier si non-vide, suivi de stdout si non-vide. Utiliser le format : `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>`. Si les deux flux sont vides, afficher `Unable to <action>: exit code N`.
       10→
       11→## User Stories
       12→
       13→1. As a developer, I want to see both stderr and stdout error messages from subprocess failures, so that I can diagnose issues more effectively without missing critical information
       14→2. As a maintainer, I want stderr to be displayed before stdout in error messages, so that error streams follow conventional logging practices
       15→3. As a tester, I want empty streams to be excluded from error messages, so that I only see relevant diagnostic information
       16→4. As a user, I want to see the exit code when both streams are empty, so that I have minimal diagnostic information for the failure
       17→5. As a developer, I want success cases to remain unchanged, so that existing behavior is preserved for non-error scenarios
       18→
       19→## Implementation Decisions
       20→
       21→- **Error message format**: `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>` with real newline character between streams
       22→- **Display order**: stderr first if non-empty, then stdout if non-empty
       23→- **Stream filtering**: Only include non-empty trimmed streams in the error message
       24→- **Fallback behavior**: `Unable to <action>: exit code N` when both stderr and stdout are empty
       25→- **Success preservation**: No changes to success case handling
       26→- **Method preservation**: All private methods and interfaces remain unchanged; no duplication, truncation, or deduplication
       27→- **File scope**: Changes limited to `acp-sandbox/src/runtime.ts` (assertSuccess) and `acp-sandbox/src/gitPromotion.ts` (requireSuccess)
       28→
       29→## Testing Decisions
       30→
       31→- **Test location**: `acp-sandbox/test/runtime.test.ts`
       32→- **Test approach**: 5 public API tests for `runCodex` using `fakeExecutor`/`sandboxScenario`

       34→  1. Two streams (both stderr and stdout non-empty)
       35→  2. Stderr only (stdout empty)
       36→  3. Stdout only (stderr empty)
       37→  4. No streams (both empty)
       38→  5. Success case (no error)
       39→- **Existing tests**: Update affected expectations in runtime and promotion tests to match new error message format
       40→- **Execution**: `npm ci` at root then `npm test` at root with real exit codes

content:         1→# Specification: Corriger diagnostics de subprocess dans assertSuccess et requireSuccess
        2→
        3→## Problem Statement
        4→
        5→Les méthodes privées `assertSuccess` (runtime.ts:681-686) et `requireSuccess` (gitPromotion.ts:523-530) masquent le stdout lorsque stderr est présent. Le code actuel utilise `result.stderr.trim() || result.stdout.trim()` qui retourne uniquement stderr si non-vide, ignorant complètement stdout même si celui-ci contient des informations diagnostiques importantes.
        6→
        7→## Solution
        8→
        9→Corriger le formatage des messages d'erreur pour afficher les deux flux (stderr et stdout) de manière distincte et complète, avec stderr en premier si non-vide, suivi de stdout si non-vide. Utiliser le format : `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>`. Si les deux flux sont vides, afficher `Unable to <action>: exit code N`.
       10→
       11→## User Stories
       12→
       13→1. As a developer, I want to see both stderr and stdout error messages from subprocess failures, so that I can diagnose issues more effectively without missing critical information
       14→2. As a maintainer, I want stderr to be displayed before stdout in error messages, so that error streams follow conventional logging practices
       15→3. As a tester, I want empty streams to be excluded from error messages, so that I only see relevant diagnostic information
       16→4. As a user, I want to see the exit code when both streams are empty, so that I have minimal diagnostic information for the failure
       17→5. As a developer, I want success cases to remain unchanged, so that existing behavior is preserved for non-error scenarios
       18→
       19→## Implementation Decisions
       20→
       21→- **Error message format**: `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>` with real newline character between streams
       22→- **Display order**: stderr first if non-empty, then stdout if non-empty
       23→- **Stream filtering**: Only include non-empty trimmed streams in the error message
       24→- **Fallback behavior**: `Unable to <action>: exit code N` when both stderr and stdout are empty
       25→- **Success preservation**: No changes to success case handling
       26→- **Method preservation**: All private methods and interfaces remain unchanged; no duplication, truncation, or deduplication
       27→- **File scope**: Changes limited to `acp-sandbox/src/runtime.ts` (assertSuccess) and `acp-sandbox/src/gitPromotion.ts` (requireSuccess)

        6→
        7→## Solution
        8→
        9→Corriger le formatage des messages d'erreur pour afficher les deux flux (stderr et stdout) de manière distincte et complète, avec stderr en premier si non-vide, suivi de stdout si non-vide. Utiliser le format : `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>`. Si les deux flux sont vides, afficher `Unable to <action>: exit code N`.
       10→
       11→## User Stories
       12→
       13→1. As a developer, I want to see both stderr and stdout error messages from subprocess failures, so that I can diagnose issues more effectively without missing critical information
       14→2. As a maintainer, I want stderr to be displayed before stdout in error messages, so that error streams follow conventional logging practices
       15→3. As a tester, I want empty streams to be excluded from error messages, so that I only see relevant diagnostic information
       16→4. As a user, I want to see the exit code when both streams are empty, so that I have minimal diagnostic information for the failure
       17→5. As a developer, I want success cases to remain unchanged, so that existing behavior is preserved for non-error scenarios

       23→- **Stream filtering**: Only include non-empty trimmed streams in the error message
       24→- **Fallback behavior**: `Unable to <action>: exit code N` when both stderr and stdout are empty

content:         1→# Specification: Corriger diagnostics de subprocess dans assertSuccess et requireSuccess
        2→
        3→## Problem Statement
        4→
        5→Les méthodes privées `assertSuccess` (runtime.ts:681-686) et `requireSuccess` (gitPromotion.ts:523-530) masquent le stdout lorsque stderr est présent. Le code actuel utilise `result.stderr.trim() || result.stdout.trim()` qui retourne uniquement stderr si non-vide, ignorant complètement stdout même si celui-ci contient des informations diagnostiques importantes.
        6→
        7→## Solution
        8→
        9→Corriger le formatage des messages d'erreur pour afficher les deux flux (stderr et stdout) de manière distincte et complète, avec stderr en premier si non-vide, suivi de stdout si non-vide. Utiliser le format : `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>`. Si les deux flux sont vides, afficher `Unable to <action>: exit code N`.
       10→
       11→## User Stories
       12→
       13→1. As a developer, I want to see both stderr and stdout error messages from subprocess failures, so that I can diagnose issues more effectively without missing critical information
       14→2. As a maintainer, I want stderr to be displayed before stdout in error messages, so that error streams follow conventional logging practices
       15→3. As a tester, I want empty streams to be excluded from error messages, so that I only see relevant diagnostic information
       16→4. As a user, I want to see the exit code when both streams are empty, so that I have minimal diagnostic information for the failure
       17→5. As a developer, I want success cases to remain unchanged, so that existing behavior is preserved for non-error scenarios
       18→
       19→## Implementation Decisions
       20→
       21→- **Error message format**: `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>` with real newline character between streams
       22→- **Display order**: stderr first if non-empty, then stdout if non-empty
       23→- **Stream filtering**: Only include non-empty trimmed streams in the error message
       24→- **Fallback behavior**: `Unable to <action>: exit code N` when both stderr and stdout are empty
       25→- **Success preservation**: No changes to success case handling
       26→- **Method preservation**: All private methods and interfaces remain unchanged; no duplication, truncation, or deduplication
       27→- **File scope**: Changes limited to `acp-sandbox/src/runtime.ts` (assertSuccess) and `acp-sandbox/src/gitPromotion.ts` (requireSuccess)
       28→
       29→## Testing Decisions
       30→
       31→- **Test location**: `acp-sandbox/test/runtime.test.ts`
       32→- **Test approach**: 5 public API tests for `runCodex` using `fakeExecutor`/`sandboxScenario`
       33→- **Test coverage**:
       34→  1. Two streams (both stderr and stdout non-empty)
       35→  2. Stderr only (stdout empty)
       36→  3. Stdout only (stderr empty)
       37→  4. No streams (both empty)
       38→  5. Success case (no error)
       39→- **Existing tests**: Update affected expectations in runtime and promotion tests to match new error message format
       40→- **Execution**: `npm ci` at root then `npm test` at root with real exit codes
       41→
       42→## Out of Scope
       43→
       44→- No changes to private/any access modifiers
       45→- No package.json/lock/dependency modifications
       46→- No ADR or glossary updates
       47→- No tail/pipefail/tsx usage
       48→- No historical audits or transcriptions
       49→- No duplication of existing functionality

Le code actuel utilise `result.stderr.trim() || result.stdout.trim()` qui retourne uniquement stderr si non-vide, ignorant complètement stdout même si celui-ci contient des informations diagnostiques importantes.
        6→
        7→## Solution
        8→
        9→Corriger le formatage des messages d'erreur pour afficher les deux flux (stderr et stdout) de manière distincte et complète, avec stderr en premier si non-vide, suivi de stdout si non-vide. Utiliser le format : `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>`. Si les deux flux sont vides, afficher `Unable to <action>: exit code N`.
       10→
       11→## User Stories
       12→
       13→1. As a developer, I want to see both stderr and stdout error messages from subprocess failures, so that I can diagnose issues more effectively without missing critical information
       14→2. As a maintainer, I want stderr to be displayed before stdout in error messages, so that error streams follow conventional logging practices
       15→3. As a tester, I want empty streams to be excluded from error messages, so that I only see relevant diagnostic information
       16→4. As a user, I want to see the exit code when both streams are empty, so that I have minimal diagnostic information for the failure
       17→5. As a developer, I want success cases to remain unchanged, so that existing behavior is preserved for non-error scenarios
       18→

       20→
       21→- **Error message format**: `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>` with real newline character between streams
       22→- **Display order**: stderr first if non-empty, then stdout if non-empty
       23→- **Stream filtering**: Only include non-empty trimmed streams in the error message
       24→- **Fallback behavior**: `Unable to <action>: exit code N` when both stderr and stdout are empty
       25→- **Success preservation**: No changes to success case handling
       26→- **Method preservation**: All private methods and interfaces remain unchanged; no duplication, truncation, or deduplication

        2→
        3→## Problem Statement
        4→
        5→Les méthodes privées `assertSuccess` (runtime.ts:681-686) et `requireSuccess` (gitPromotion.ts:523-530) masquent le stdout lorsque stderr est présent. Le code actuel utilise `result.stderr.trim() || result.stdout.trim()` qui retourne uniquement stderr si non-vide, ignorant complètement stdout même si celui-ci contient des informations diagnostiques importantes.
        6→
        7→## Solution
        8→
        9→Corriger le formatage des messages d'erreur pour afficher les deux flux (stderr et stdout) de manière distincte et complète, avec stderr en premier si non-vide, suivi de stdout si non-vide. Utiliser le format : `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>`. Si les deux flux sont vides, afficher `Unable to <action>: exit code N`.
       10→
       11→## User Stories
       12→
       13→1. As a developer, I want to see both stderr and stdout error messages from subprocess failures, so that I can diagnose issues more effectively without missing critical information
       14→2. As a maintainer, I want stderr to be displayed before stdout in error messages, so that error streams follow conventional logging practices
       15→3. As a tester, I want empty streams to be excluded from error messages, so that I only see relevant diagnostic information
       16→4. As a user, I want to see the exit code when both streams are empty, so that I have minimal diagnostic information for the failure
       17→5. As a developer, I want success cases to remain unchanged, so that existing behavior is preserved for non-error scenarios
       18→
       19→## Implementation Decisions
       20→
       21→- **Error message format**: `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>` with real newline character between streams
       22→- **Display order**: stderr first if non-empty, then stdout if non-empty
       23→- **Stream filtering**: Only include non-empty trimmed streams in the error message
       24→- **Fallback behavior**: `Unable to <action>: exit code N` when both stderr and stdout are empty
       25→- **Success preservation**: No changes to success case handling
       26→- **Method preservation**: All private methods and interfaces remain unchanged; no duplication, truncation, or deduplication

        4→

        6→
        7→## Solution
        8→
        9→Corriger le formatage des messages d'erreur pour afficher les deux flux (stderr et stdout) de manière distincte et complète, avec stderr en premier si non-vide, suivi de stdout si non-vide.        13→1. As a developer, I want to see both stderr and stdout error messages from subprocess failures, so that I can diagnose issues more effectively without missing critical information

       15→3. As a tester, I want empty streams to be excluded from error messages, so that I only see relevant diagnostic information
       16→4. As a user, I want to see the exit code when both streams are empty, so that I have minimal diagnostic information for the failure

       15→3. As a tester, I want empty streams to be excluded from error messages, so that I only see relevant diagnostic information
       16→4. As a user, I want to see the exit code when both streams are empty, so that I have minimal diagnostic information for the failure

        2→
        3→## Problem Statement
        4→
        5→Les méthodes privées `assertSuccess` (runtime.ts:681-686) et `requireSuccess` (gitPromotion.ts:523-530) masquent le stdout lorsque stderr est présent. Le code actuel utilise `result.stderr.trim() || result.stdout.trim()` qui retourne uniquement stderr si non-vide, ignorant complètement stdout même si celui-ci contient des informations diagnostiques importantes.
        6→
        7→## Solution
        8→
        9→Corriger le formatage des messages d'erreur pour afficher les deux flux (stderr et stdout) de manière distincte et complète, avec stderr en premier si non-vide, suivi de stdout si non-vide. Utiliser le format : `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>`. Si les deux flux sont vides, afficher `Unable to <action>: exit code N`.
       10→
       11→## User Stories
       12→
       13→1. As a developer, I want to see both stderr and stdout error messages from subprocess failures, so that I can diagnose issues more effectively without missing critical information
       14→2. As a maintainer, I want stderr to be displayed before stdout in error messages, so that error streams follow conventional logging practices
       15→3. As a tester, I want empty streams to be excluded from error messages, so that I only see relevant diagnostic information
       16→4. As a user, I want to see the exit code when both streams are empty, so that I have minimal diagnostic information for the failure
       17→5. As a developer, I want success cases to remain unchanged, so that existing behavior is preserved for non-error scenarios
       18→

       20→
       21→- **Error message format**: `Unable to <action>: [stderr] <trimmed_message>\n[stdout] <trimmed_message>` with real newline character between streams
       22→- **Display order**: stderr first if non-empty, then stdout if non-empty
       23→- **Stream filtering**: Only include non-empty trimmed streams in the error message
       24→- **Fallback behavior**: `Unable to <action>: exit code N` when both stderr and stdout are empty
       25→- **Success preservation**: No changes to success case handling
       26→- **Method preservation**: All private methods and interfaces remain unchanged; no duplication, truncation, or deduplication
